answers.core: Collision detection is one of the most basic aspects of any game with moving parts.
answers.workaround:
Kind of? There's the direct space physics query API ([2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_physicsdirectspacestate2d.html)/[3D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_physicsdirectspacestate3d.html)), but that has performance issues in part due to the use of Dictionaries. It's also not very ergonomic.

There's also the `ShapeCast3D` node but it's also awkward to use and might have its own performance problems (needing to set `enabled` to false and repeatedly call `force_shapecast_update` for updated results, and these results include multiple collisions when only one is necessary).

Also if the user wants to just use `move_and_slide` there isn't an alternative currently.
